requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
I read the supplied tests and did not request any implementation source. Together they cover each obligation of `requirements.references.outline_comments`.

- **Profile-defined comments, Markdown.**
  - `fn[markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments]` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` asserts that only the block comment is a comment (`outline.comments.len() == 1`).
  - It also asserts that the inline `<!-- inline -->` lies in no comment span and that its line's owner is a `paragraph` node under `section[H]`.
  - The block comment belongs to the following `section[Sub]`.

- **Consecutive comment lines form one run, and a run belongs to the next node starting after it in its container.**
  - `fn[comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next]` checks a two-line `// one` / `// two` run before `fn b`, and both lines go to `fn[b]`.
  - `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers a run before `third` that is separated from it by a blank line, and a run before a nested `fn inner`.
  - `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` repeats the rule for Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. Its Python case uses a two-line run (`lead one` / `lead two`).

- **Container fallback and root.**
  - When the container has no later node, the run belongs to the container. `fn[trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod]`, the `// alone in m` and `// inside third` cases, and the `after m` / `after b` cases in the per-language test cover this.
  - At top level the run belongs to the root. `fn[top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root]`, the `// final` case, and the per-language `tail` cases cover this.

- **Trailing comments.**
  - A comment that follows other source on its line forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing that line. `fn[comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node]` covers a trailing comment after `fn a() {}`, one inside a body, and one after a closing brace (`closing b` goes to `fn[b]`, `closing m` goes to `mod[m]`).
  - The following standalone `// before b` run is separate and goes to `fn[b]`.
  - `fn[a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run]` covers the "including another comment" case. `first` goes to `fn[b]`, and `second` goes to the root because no node contains that line.
  - Trailing-comment cases appear in every language of the per-language test.

- **Rust inner doc comments bind to their container.**
  - `fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` checks `//!` and `/*! */` at file level, and both go to the root.
  - `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` checks `//! Module docs.` inside `mod m`, which belongs to `mod[m]`.
  - In the same test, the ordinary comment `// above inner` directly after those docs goes to `fn[inner]`. So an ordinary comment and an inner doc comment are not merged into one run.
  - `fn[distinct_runs_with_the_same_owner_do_not_close_each_others_fences]` in `src/fenced.rs` also covers the run boundary between inner docs and an ordinary comment.

- **YAML.** `fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` and `fn[workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows]` check comments before a nested key.

- **A reference in a comment counts for its run's node.**
  - `fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` and `fn[reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node]` in `src/evidence.rs` cover this.
  - `fn[comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run]` in `src/fenced.rs` and `fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` cover it too.
  - `fn[search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners]` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` and the structural and search owner tests (`fn[matches_belong_to_the_innermost_node_or_comment_owner]`, `fn[search_ranges_resolve_to_comment_owners_or_the_common_enclosing_item]`) check owner resolution through consumers.

- **MAY clause.** The permission for a profile to bind a comment kind to its container imposes nothing to test beyond the required Rust binding. That binding is tested.

- **Cited requirements.** Application under `requirements.references.coverage.tests` is tested in `fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]`. Application under `requirements.references.authoring_inputs` is tested in `fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]`. Both assert the owner node or its effect.

I found no plausible violation that these assertions would accept, and no unacknowledged gap.

:::{req} coverage.tests
Every Rust function carrying a test attribute, `#[test]` or an attribute whose
path ends in `test` such as `#[tokio::test]`, including those in Cargo
integration-test targets, MUST carry a `{test}` reference to a requirement or
named example under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`, in a comment
attached to it or within its body. A test function without one MUST be a
validation error naming its file, line, and name.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
